Generate an Alluvial Plot from a Long-Format Data Frame

Source: R/alluvial_plot.R
alluvial_plot.Rd

This function generates an alluvial plot using a long-format data frame where microbial abundances are plotted across categorical variables (axes). It supports both relative and absolute abundance types, filters based on abundance thresholds, and allows for displaying the top taxa. Additional customization options include faceting, custom colors, and setting the legend. The function supports displaying multiple axes or plotting without axes when axes = NULL.

alluvial_plot(
  data,
  axes = NULL,
  abundance_threshold = 10000,
  fill_variable = "Phylum",
  silent = TRUE,
  abundance_type = "absolute",
  total_reads = NULL,
  top_taxa = NULL,
  facet_vars = NULL,
  text_size = 4,
  legend_ncol = 1,
  custom_colors = color_palette$MG,
  color_mapping = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing microbial data, including abundance and categorical variables.

axes

A character vector specifying the axes (columns) to include in the alluvial plot. If NULL, no axes will be shown on the x-axis.

abundance_threshold

A numeric value specifying the minimum abundance threshold for including samples. Default is 10000 for absolute abundance and a relative threshold for relative abundance (e.g., 0.001 for 0.1%).

fill_variable

A character string specifying the variable to use for the fill color in the alluvial plot. Default is "Phylum".

silent

A logical indicating whether to suppress messages from ggalluvial::is_alluvia_form. Default is TRUE.

abundance_type

A character string specifying whether to plot "relative" or "absolute" abundance. Default is "absolute".

total_reads

A numeric value specifying the total number of reads for relative abundance calculation. Default is NULL.

top_taxa

An integer specifying the number of top taxa to display. Default is NULL, meaning all taxa will be displayed.

facet_vars

A character vector specifying variables for faceting. Default is NULL (no faceting).

text_size

A numeric value specifying the size of the text labels inside the plot. Default is 4.

legend_ncol

An integer specifying the number of columns for the legend. Default is 1.

custom_colors

A character vector specifying custom colors for the fill variable. Can use color_palette$MG or color_palette$extended_palette. Default is color_palette$MG.

color_mapping

A named character vector specifying specific colors for taxa. Default is NULL.

Value

A ggplot2 object representing the alluvial plot.

Details

The function uses the ggalluvial package to construct the plot and relies on ggplot2 for customization.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example data
data(physeq_16SOTU)  # Replace with actual data loading
pps_Abs <- phyloseq::psmelt(physeq_16SOTU)

# Example of total reads calculation for relative abundance
total_reads <- sum(pps_Abs$Abundance)

# Generate an alluvial plot using the extended palette
alluvial_plot_abs <- alluvial_plot(
  data = pps_Abs, 
  axes = c("Env.broad.scale", "Host.genus", "Diet"), 
  abundance_threshold = 10000, 
  fill_variable = "Phylum", 
  silent = TRUE, 
  abundance_type = "absolute", 
  top_taxa = 10, 
  text_size = 4, 
  legend_ncol = 1, 
  custom_colors = color_palette$extended_palette  # Use the extended palette from your package
)

# Print the alluvial plot for absolute abundance
print(alluvial_plot_abs)
} # }
